prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin to establish rules on which kinds of change work or fail, as each kind of change has only one test so far.
Predictions were too high for failed tests: both [adoption, redesign] (predicted +14.0%, actual -7.4%) and [sign_in, reorder] (predicted +6.0%, actual -7.4%) yielded negative results.
Predictions were too low for winning tests: [finish, redesign] exceeded expectations (predicted +3.0%, actual +5.0%).

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: -7.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, redesign: +5.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -7.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 69.7%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 19.2%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [choose_path, redesign] Interactive Story Scroll Path Choice: Redesign the story screen into an interactive story scroll layout with mascot presentation to engage users before path selection. (why: Choose path drop-off is 23.8% with a high mean time of 514s, suggesting users feel unengaged or hesitant at the start.)
1: [finish, new_screen] Desktop Interaction Modes Screen: Add a dedicated post-intro screen explaining primary pet interaction controls such as tray positioning and chat. (why: 3 support emails reported confusion regarding how to control, hide, or talk to their pet after finishing setup.)
2: [adoption, new_flow] Live Breed Selection Carousel: Transform companion selection into an interactive audio-visual carousel experience. (why: Adoption step has a high drop-off rate of 39.1% and a long mean time of 1017s.)
3: [home, redesign] Progressive Waiting Status Checklist: Rebuild the waiting screen with a live stage-by-stage checklist layout showing pet generation progress. (why: The waiting phase has a median time of 201s and mean of 2336s, causing user drop-off while waiting without feedback.)
4: [sign_in, copy] Account Synchronization Benefit Copy: Update sign in copy to explicitly state that account sign-in backs up and synchronizes pet data to cloud. (why: 8 support emails cited missing or reset pets after signing in again, showing confusion around account persistence.)
5: [choose_path, hint] Path Decision Speed Hint: Display a helpful hint on path selection explaining that companion choices can be changed later in app settings. (why: Choose path mean time is 514s compared to 8s median, showing a long tail of users struggling to decide.)
6: [home, wait_info] Waiting Screen Entertainment Tips: Add an engaging tip carousel to the waiting screen that displays pet care advice while files render. (why: Waiting step takes a median of 201s, during which disengaged users leave or assume the app froze.)
7: [finish, notification] Desktop Visibility Confirmation Toast: Add a clear status hint on the home intro screen letting users know where on their desktop screen the pet is placed. (why: 3 support emails reported that the pet did not show up on the desktop after completing onboarding.)

scores.note: Targeted step has 23.8% drop, but flow redesigns carry high risk and high cost without support mail confirmation.
Strong evidence from 3 support emails on finish step, but adding a new screen requires release and build effort.
Highest drop-off step (39.1%), but past adoption redesign failed (-7.4%) and cost is high.
Addresses high median wait time (201s), but requires major UI layout rebuild.
8 support emails directly address this issue; copy change is config-only with high potential ROI.
Low cost hint targeted at high mean time (514s vs 8s median) to reduce decision hesitation.
Engages users during 201s median wait with low risk of breaking conversion flow.
Strong support mail alignment, simple toast component, and finish step changes previously succeeded.
